backlog.spec: Append the full RDKit physchem descriptor set (Descriptors.descList, about 200 values: MolWt, TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, aromatic ring counts, fraction sp3, and so on) to the existing 2048-bit Morgan vector in featurize. Replace NaN and inf with 0 and clip extreme values to the 1st and 99th percentiles of the training set. Keep the random forest otherwise unchanged.
backlog.title: RDKit 2D descriptor block added to Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Instead of the full bit vector, featurize each molecule with about 15 interpretable descriptors that drive passive permeability: TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count, formal charge of ionizable groups (carboxylic acid, basic amine counts via SMARTS), fraction sp3, heavy atom count, and ring count. Fit the same random forest on this compact table. Compact descriptors often generalize better to unseen scaffolds than sparse fingerprints.
backlog.title: Small curated physchem feature set

backlog.spec: Replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same Morgan generator so each feature holds the number of times a substructure occurs rather than a 0/1 flag. Keep radius 2 and 2048 length. The random forest is unchanged apart from the input.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprint instead of bits

backlog.spec: Build the fingerprint with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator using an atom invariant generator for feature invariants (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen) so that the bits encode donor, acceptor, aromatic, and ionizable pharmacophore classes. Use radius 2 and 2048 bits. Retain the random forest.
backlog.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP) pharmacophore fingerprint

backlog.spec: Build one feature vector per molecule by concatenating four fingerprints: Morgan radius 2 counts (1024 bits), MACCS keys (167 bits from rdMolDescriptors.GetMACCSKeysFingerprint), RDKit topological torsion counts (1024 bits), and atom-pair counts (1024 bits). Use the same random forest on the concatenated matrix.
backlog.title: Concatenate several fingerprint types

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan features with MACCS structural keys (rdMolDescriptors.GetMACCSKeysFingerprint, 167 bits). MACCS covers broad functional-group presence, which may transfer better across skeletons than radius-2 hashed environments. Keep the random forest hyperparameters the same.
backlog.title: MACCS keys alone with random forest

backlog.spec: Swap the random forest for a LightGBM regressor (LGBMRegressor) with about 600 trees, learning rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, and random_state set from seed. Keep the Morgan 2048-bit features. Use the L2 objective.
backlog.title: LightGBM regressor on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the random forest with CatBoostRegressor, depth 6, about 800 iterations, learning rate 0.05, l2_leaf_reg 3, random_seed set from seed, verbose off, thread_count 8. Train on the Morgan 2048-bit matrix. Ordered boosting usually resists overfitting on small datasets like this one.
backlog.title: CatBoost regressor on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Use XGBRegressor with max_depth 6, n_estimators 600, learning_rate 0.03, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 2, tree_method hist, and random_state=seed. Input is the Morgan 2048-bit matrix. Predict the test molecules directly.
backlog.title: XGBoost regressor on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard) similarity matrix between Morgan bit vectors of train and test molecules, that is K = (A·B) / (|A| + |B| - A·B) using numpy. Fit sklearn SVR with kernel='precomputed', C around 5, epsilon 0.05. Predict with the test-by-train similarity matrix. Chemically motivated kernel models often beat forests on small data.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression

backlog.spec: Build the Tanimoto similarity kernel on Morgan bit vectors as in a precomputed kernel. Fit sklearn's GaussianProcessRegressor with a fixed kernel of the form signal_variance * K_tanimoto plus a WhiteKernel noise term, normalize_y=True, and alpha 1e-2. Predict the test mean. Compare with SVR for uncertainty-aware smoothing.
backlog.title: Gaussian process with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity between each test molecule and all training molecules over Morgan bit vectors. Predict as the similarity-weighted average of the k=5 most similar training targets, with weights equal to similarity raised to power 2. This nonparametric baseline is cheap and can be blended with the forest.
backlog.title: k-nearest-neighbour regression on Tanimoto similarity

backlog.spec: Standardize the combined Morgan count features and RDKit descriptors (StandardScaler fit on training only, NaN replaced with 0). Fit sklearn Ridge with alpha chosen from [1, 3, 10, 30] by an inner 3-fold GroupKFold-free KFold on the training set, scored by MAE. Output the ridge predictions.
backlog.title: Ridge regression on fingerprints plus descriptors

backlog.spec: Train an MLPRegressor from sklearn with hidden_layer_sizes (512, 128), activation relu, solver adam, learning_rate_init 1e-3, alpha 1e-3 (L2), early_stopping True with validation_fraction 0.15, max_iter 300, random_state=seed. Input is the Morgan 2048-bit matrix, and the target is standardized using the training mean and standard deviation before fitting.
backlog.title: MLP on fingerprints with Adam

backlog.spec: Because the metric is mean absolute error, train the gradient-boosted model with an absolute-error objective (LightGBM objective='l1', or sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor loss='absolute_error'). The predicted value then targets the conditional median, which lowers MAE on skewed residuals. Keep the Morgan 2048-bit input.
backlog.title: Optimize for MAE with quantile or absolute-loss boosting

backlog.spec: Keep the random forest, but after fitting, replace each prediction with the median of the training targets in the leaves a test molecule reaches. Implement by calling model.apply on training and test matrices, collecting for each tree the training-sample indices per leaf, and taking the median of their targets across trees. Median aggregation matches the MAE objective.
backlog.title: Random forest with MAE-friendly leaf median

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with objective='huber' and alpha set to about 1.0 (the Huber threshold in log-permeability units), otherwise as in the LightGBM setup. Huber is a compromise between squared error and absolute error, and it limits the pull of large-residual outliers in the Caco-2 labels.
backlog.title: Huber loss boosting for outlier robustness

backlog.spec: Keep the random forest but tune regularization: set min_samples_leaf to 3, max_features to 0.2, and max_depth to None. Increase n_estimators to 500. Larger leaves smooth predictions and reduce overfitting to specific skeletons in the training folds.
backlog.title: Stronger forest regularization via leaf size and feature sampling

backlog.spec: Modify the random forest so that bootstrap=True with max_samples=0.6. Subsampling rows per tree decorrelates trees and reduces variance on this small dataset. Keep the other forest settings. This is a single-parameter change designed to reduce variance on unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Bootstrap subsample rate and max_samples tuning

backlog.spec: Fit two models on the same Morgan features, a random forest (300 trees) and a LightGBM regressor (about 500 trees, learning rate 0.03, feature_fraction 0.3). Return the simple average of their test predictions. Averaging models of different bias reduces error more than either alone.
backlog.title: Averaging forest and gradient boosting ensemble

backlog.spec: Train three random forests with seeds seed, seed+1, seed+2, each with 200 trees, and average their predictions. This reduces the variance from bootstrap randomness that the harness noise sd partly reflects. The features and hyperparameters stay the same.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged random forest ensemble

backlog.spec: Build out-of-fold predictions on the training set with an inner 5-fold KFold for three base models (random forest, LightGBM, SVR on the Tanimoto kernel). Fit a non-negative linear regression (scipy nnls or sklearn LinearRegression with positive=True) on the out-of-fold predictions. Apply base models refit on the full training set to the test molecules and combine them with the learned weights.
backlog.title: Stacking with a ridge meta-learner

backlog.spec: Post-process the random forest output by shrinking predictions toward the training median: final = median + lambda * (pred - median) with lambda 0.9. Forests tend to be overconfident on unseen skeletons, and mild shrinkage can lower MAE. Choose lambda by an inner validation split of the training data.
backlog.title: Target shrinkage toward training median

backlog.spec: Give each training molecule a sample weight equal to the inverse count of molecules sharing its Murcko scaffold within the training fold (computed with MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles), normalized to mean 1. Pass the weights to RandomForestRegressor.fit via sample_weight. This stops heavily repeated scaffolds from dominating the fit.
backlog.title: Sample-weight by molecular size or scaffold frequency

backlog.spec: Before featurizing, strip salts and counterions by keeping the largest fragment from Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags, neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and drop explicit stereochemistry with Chem.RemoveStereochemistry. Fall back to the original molecule if parsing fails. This standardization can reduce noise from mixture entries in the Caco-2 data.
backlog.title: Clean inputs: largest fragment and salt stripping

backlog.spec: Train on a transformed target and invert it at prediction time. The labels are already log-scale, so try a centered transform: fit on (y - mean(y)) scaled by its standard deviation, then rescale predictions back. This standardizes the scale for models with fixed regularization strength such as SVR and the MLP. Random forest outputs are unchanged by linear scaling, so this matters mainly for the kernel and MLP models.
backlog.title: Log-target and sqrt-target transform

backlog.spec: For each training molecule, generate additional SMILES with Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True, canonical=False) using a seed-derived random generator, up to 4 variants each. Featurize all variants with the same labels. Average test predictions over the canonical and randomized test SMILES. For count-based fingerprints the augmented rows are mostly redundant, so use this with the forest only if it helps.
backlog.title: Data augmentation by randomized SMILES

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training set with an inner KFold of 4 folds, and evaluate a small grid over max_features in {0.1, 0.3, 0.5} and min_samples_leaf in {1, 3, 5} using MAE. Refit the random forest with the best pair on all training data. Keep runtime under budget by using 200 trees during the search and the final fit with 400.
backlog.title: Hyperparameter search for random forest inside fit_predict

backlog.spec: Hold out 10 percent of the training molecules as an internal validation set inside fit_predict. Train LightGBM with objective='l1' and up to 2000 rounds using early_stopping(100) on the validation MAE. Refit on all training data with the best iteration count scaled by 1.1. This tunes the number of boosting rounds per fold instead of fixing it.
backlog.title: Early stopping for LightGBM via internal validation

backlog.spec: Train a small PyTorch-free MLP in numpy or via sklearn partial_fit over 200 epochs with a cosine learning-rate decay from 1e-3 to 1e-5, batch size 32, and Adam-style updates. Input is the Morgan count features. Use MAE loss so the optimization target matches the metric. Only use this if the sklearn MLP is not enough.
backlog.title: Cosine decay learning rate for the MLP
